comparator.name: Data Science and Society
comparator.sourceNotes: This example follows the AI and Society specialization. It includes a field project in the second year and a 30 EC minor and 15 EC thesis in the third year.

components.name: Introduction to Data Science and Society
components.note: Introduces data science and its social context.

components.name: Programming for Data Science
components.note: Introduces programming for working with data.

components.name: Science and Technology Studies I
components.note: Examines relationships between science, technology and society.

components.name: Governance and Regulation of Innovation I: Introduction
components.note: Introduces governance and regulation of innovation.

components.name: Statistical and Machine Learning
components.note: Introduces statistical learning and machine learning.

components.name: Visualising Data
components.note: Develops visual ways to communicate data.

components.name: Human Rights in the Digital Age I: Human Dignity
components.note: Examines human dignity and rights in digital settings.

components.name: Science and Technology Studies II
components.note: Continues the study of science, technology and society.

components.name: Statistical Inference
components.note: Draws conclusions from data using statistical inference.

components.name: Data Science I: Databases and Data Sources
components.note: Studies databases and data sources.

components.name: Data Science II: Big Data Analytics
components.note: Studies the analysis of large datasets.

components.name: Governance and Regulation of Innovation II: Responsibility
components.note: Examines responsibility in innovation.

components.name: Data Science III: Using Data to Solve Social Problems
components.note: Uses data to investigate social problems.

components.name: Data Science IV: Using Data to Solve Business Problems
components.note: Uses data to investigate business problems.

components.name: Human Rights in the Digital Age II: Reconsidering Impact
components.note: Examines how digital systems affect rights.

components.name: Data Science V: Visual Rhetoric
components.note: Studies how visual choices shape the interpretation of data.

components.name: Governance and Regulation of Innovation III: Sustainability
components.note: Studies innovation and sustainability.

components.name: Simulation Exercise
components.note: Uses simulation to explore decision-making.

components.name: Field Project
components.note: Develops a data project with researchers and a public or private organization.

components.name: AI Advanced Skills I
components.note: Introduces deep learning architectures and workflows.

components.name: AI Ethics and Politics
components.note: Examines the ethical and political dimensions of AI.

components.name: AI Advanced Skills II
components.note: Applies deep learning to problems such as language modeling.

components.name: AI Regulation
components.note: Studies rules and approaches for governing AI.

components.name: Minor
components.note: Students choose an approved minor.

components.name: Advanced Programming
components.note: Develops advanced programming techniques.

components.name: Research Design and Project Management
components.note: Develops research design and project planning.

components.note: A supervised, independent research project.

The Cognitive Technology specialization supports a second, distinct direction. Business data and visual communication are integrated components of the common curriculum and are covered within the selected directions.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop programming skills. UCR focuses on Python and computational problem-solving.
Both study how data are organized and retrieved. UCR focuses on relational modeling and SQL.
Both use visualizations to explore and communicate data. UCR also teaches data cleaning and analysis.
Both use statistical and machine learning methods for prediction and model evaluation.
Both develop neural network methods, from foundational architectures to more advanced applications.
Both develop probability and statistical inference.
Groningen combines data science and its social context in one introductory course.
Groningen has a dedicated big data analytics course. UCR develops advanced analysis through machine learning and neural networks.
Groningen studies the rhetoric of data graphics. UCR develops visual analysis and data visualization in separate settings.
Groningen has a dedicated advanced programming course. UCR develops programming through several computational courses.
Both examine foundations of human rights. UCR covers general rights theory and legal protections.
Both examine AI ethics and public consequences, including fairness, privacy and accountability.
Both apply research and data analysis to business questions. UCR focuses on customers and markets.
Groningen studies science and technology as social practices. UCR addresses social institutions and technology across courses.
Groningen continues its science and technology studies sequence.
Groningen has a dedicated course on governance of innovation.
Groningen studies responsibility in innovation. UCR addresses related questions through AI ethics and organizational study.
Groningen applies human rights to digital impacts in a second dedicated course.
Groningen applies data science directly to social problems. UCR develops data analysis and social research through separate courses.
Groningen studies sustainability in its innovation-governance sequence.
Groningen studies AI regulation as a dedicated subject.
Groningen uses a dedicated simulation exercise. UCR applies computational models to decision problems.
Groningen applies advanced AI to problems such as language modeling. UCR also studies text classification and generation in its neural networks course.
Groningen has a dedicated human–machine interaction course. UCR studies related questions through cognition, perception and AI.
Both develop research design. UCR includes measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments.
Groningen requires a 10 EC field project.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for an approved minor.
Groningen requires a 15 EC thesis. UCR’s optional research element is outside the scheduled degree.
